title: Leith jet-pack drops swing from 4 to 31 minutes as sea wind bites
subtitle: Minutes from pickup to doorstep, seven Edinburgh districts, October 2026
points: Leith runs from 4 to 31 minutes, while no inland district's middle half spans more than three minutes.
Gusts over 30 knots off the Firth of Forth pin pilots to the harbour wall for up to 20 minutes.
Granton, on the same shore, swings almost as far: its slowest drop took 27 minutes against a median of 13.
From November, routing every Leith drop inland through the sheltered Pilrig corridor should cap the slowest at 18 minutes.

title: Six stages take the robot gardeners from one test street to 4,000 gardens
subtitle: Rollout plan, 2026 to 2029
bar: Protect the weed swarm: it lifts the monthly plan from £39 to £58, and the 3,200-garden break-even rests on that price

items.label: Mow the test street
items.text: Twelve robot mowers keep 40 Leeds lawns striped all summer. Not one garden gnome is lost in action, and the neighbours start asking for a robot of their own.

items.label: Teach the hedge bot
items.text: The trimmer learns nine hedge shapes, from box to beech. Topiary peacocks stay an optional extra at £6 a bird, and they sell out by the end of May.

items.label: Open three cities
items.text: Leeds, York and Bristol reach 600 gardens on a £39 monthly plan, each city run from one charging shed staffed by two humans and a well-used kettle.

items.label: Release the weed swarm
items.text: Palm-sized weeders patrol the beds overnight and cut herbicide use by 90%. Gardeners pay for the quiet, and the plan rises from £39 to £58 a month.

items.label: Add autumn leaf duty
items.text: Leaf-blowing drones clear every lawn on Tuesdays from October, keeping the fleet earning through the winter months when the mowers would sit idle.

items.label: Reach 4,000 gardens
items.text: Nine cities pass the 3,200-garden break-even with a year to spare, and the robot fleet now mows its own depot lawn on cheap overnight power.

title: First guests circle an asteroid in December 2028, if the heat shield passes
subtitle: Six dates from hangar to maiden cruise, March 2027 to December 2028
bar: Fund a second heat shield now: it costs less than a year's delay and protects the December 2028 date.

items.label: Hull fitted out
items.text: The cruiser gets 40 cabins with round windows, a glass viewing deck and a galley where the soup stays in the bowl.

items.label: Heat shield test
items.text: Three re-entry burns in a row at full heat. A single crack sends the shield back to the workshop for a year, and the launch with it.

items.label: Crew certified
items.text: Twelve pilots and guides log 200 hours each in the zero-g simulator, including the drill for a guest who will not stop somersaulting.

items.label: Sea trials, in space
items.text: An empty loop round the Moon proves the route, the oxygen budget and the coffee machine, with a test dummy in every cabin.

items.label: Tickets go on sale
items.text: 120 seats a month at launch prices, enough to sell out the first season inside a week if the trial footage looks good.

items.label: Maiden cruise
items.text: Nine days out, two slow laps of a small asteroid at a safe distance, and home in time for New Year's Eve.
